parsed.explanation: The parent regime imposes universal, traveller-facing exposures: passports and visas must reflect birth-assigned sex, X markers are barred, a consular case-note tag flags suspected trans applicants, and officers can pursue lifetime fraud findings where documents or presentation 'cast doubt' on sex. This reaches every trans visitor at every border crossing and cannot be passed or talked around; foreign governments have issued advisories and foreign trans citizens have been detained over visa issues. Custody harm is documented (forced labour, beatings, sexual abuse in immigration detention; prison hormone removal), and the state layer adds a comprehensive birth-sex statute covering bathrooms, shelters, dormitories and prisons, with no statewide anti-discrimination protection, a religious-refusal statute, and an arrest under a bathroom law recorded nationally. Remedies are partial and contested in court. Tier-1 universal exposure with thin functioning recourse, though not the systematic raids, extortion or near-automatic imprisonment of the 0.25 band; compares to the 0.35 anchors, pulled slightly lower by the border-regime breadth and documented visitor detentions.
